Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable goshs exposure: process launched with --webdav and --no-delete (<= v2.1.3)
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] WebDAV MOVE succeeds (201/204) against goshs --no-delete server · [LLM] WebDAV --no-delete probe: 403 DELETE then successful MOVE on same path · [LLM] WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite:T header (destructive RemoveAll on destination)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] goshs running --no-delete deletes/renames files on disk (CVE-2026-64863 MOVE bypass)
goshs running --no-delete deletes/renames files on disk (CVE-2026-64863 MOVE bypass) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the actual data-loss primitive: a goshs process launched with the --no-delete guard that nonetheless performs file rename/delete operations on disk. Under the CVE, a WebDAV MOVE renames (deletes) the source and, with Overwrite:T, RemoveAll's the destination — so any FileDeleted/FileRenamed initiated by a goshs '--no-delete' instance is the bypass executing. Rationale: Binds the two article-specific strings that together prove exploitation: the process image 'goshs' AND the '--no-delete' flag it was launched with, correlated to an actual FileDeleted/FileRenamed. A no-delete instance deleting files is the CVE by definition — near-zero benign overlap.
ATT&CKT1485 T1070.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator legitimately using the goshs UPLOAD or unrestricted mode (no --no-delete flag) — excluded by the cmdline filter
  • goshs writing/overwriting freshly uploaded files in an allowed upload dir (FileWritten, not delete)
  • Antivirus/EDR quarantining a file goshs just wrote, showing as a delete on the same path
  • Log-rotation or temp-file cleanup by a wrapper script that happens to share the goshs working dir
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--upload-only","-uo") and ActionType == "FileCreated")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the goshs cmdline actually contains --no-delete and identify the deleted/renamed FolderPath+PreviousFolderPath — a rename to an unrelated name or a delete of a served artifact confirms abuse. 2) Contain: stop the goshs service and block its listening WebDAV port at the host firewall; snapshot the served directory for recovery. 3) Hunt: pull the WebDAV access log for MOVE requests around the file event, extract source IPs, and search for the same client issuing PROPFIND enumeration or repeated MOVE calls across other goshs hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "goshs"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileDeleted")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, PreviousFolderPath, FileName, PreviousFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "goshs"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: goshs --no-delete Instance Deleting Files On Disk (CVE-2026-64863)
id: 2f8c1a4e-6b3d-4c9a-9f2e-1a7b0c5d8e31
status: experimental
description: A goshs process started with the --no-delete guard performing a file delete/rename, indicating the WebDAV MOVE bypass (CVE-2026-64863) destroying protected files.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hq33-8jgp-8qq3
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/04
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1485
  - attack.t1070.004
logsource:
  category: file_delete
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/goshs'
      - '\goshs.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd @process.name:goshs @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH)
#event_simpleName=/^File(Deleted|Written)$/ ContextImageFileName=/goshs/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, #event_simpleName], function=count())
| count > 0
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action IN ("deleted","renamed","modified")) Filesystem.process_name=goshs* by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action IN ("deleted","renamed","modified")) Filesystem.process_name=goshs* by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - lastTime
WebDAV MOVE succeeds (201/204) against goshs --no-delete server AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the wire-side signature of the bypass: a WebDAV MOVE verb returning 201 Created or 204 No Content. Under a correctly enforced --no-delete policy MOVE should be 403; a successful MOVE is the source-file deletion (rename) primitive the CVE exposes on the goshs WebDAV port. Rationale: Keys on the exact article verb+status: MOVE returning 201/204. Successful WebDAV MOVE is rare in most estates and is the documented deletion primitive; scoping to the goshs host (by DstIpAddr/port) turns it high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WebDAV clients (macOS Finder, Windows Explorer web folders, Cyberduck) that use MOVE for normal rename operations on an intended-writable share
  • A goshs instance intentionally run WITHOUT --no-delete where MOVE is expected
  • Backup or sync tooling that stages files via MOVE/rename over WebDAV
  • Automated CI artifact reorganisation against a non-protected goshs endpoint
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm DstIpAddr/port is a goshs --no-delete instance (check the host's process cmdline) and inspect the MOVE Url + Destination to see which served file was renamed away. 2) Contain: restrict the WebDAV port to trusted source IPs or take goshs offline until upgraded past v2.1.3. 3) Hunt: from the source IP, enumerate all MOVE/DELETE/PROPFIND to the same host and correlate to host-side FileDeleted events (see the goshs file-deletion UC) to confirm data loss.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "MOVE"
| where toint(HttpStatusCode) in (201, 204)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WebDAV --no-delete probe: 403 DELETE then successful MOVE on same path AIExploitation High
Detects the exploit's discovery-to-abuse pivot described verbatim in the advisory: DELETE is blocked (403) but MOVE on the same resource succeeds. Correlating a 403 DELETE followed within 60s by a 201/204 MOVE on the identical URL from the same client is the bypass signature. Rationale: Directly encodes the advisory's stated asymmetry ('DELETE is correctly blocked (403) but MOVE still destroys files') as a same-URL, same-client 403-DELETE→2xx-MOVE temporal correlation — an operational sequence with essentially no benign explanation.
ATT&CKT1190 T1211
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A WebDAV client that retries a failed delete as a rename by design (rare, but some sync tools fall back)
  • Two unrelated users hitting the same URL where one's DELETE is denied by ACL and another legitimately renames — mitigated by same-SrcIpAddr join
  • Load-balancer health probes issuing method variety (won't produce 403+2xx on same file path)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request sequence from SrcIpAddr to DstHostname — a 403 DELETE immediately followed by a 2xx MOVE on the same Url is a deliberate probe; note the Destination header target. 2) Contain: block SrcIpAddr at the WAF/proxy and restrict the goshs WebDAV port; preserve the served directory for recovery. 3) Hunt: sweep all goshs hosts for the same source IP and for host-side FileDeleted/FileRenamed by goshs to quantify data destroyed.
let win = 60s;
let moves = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "MOVE" and toint(HttpStatusCode) in (201,204)
    | project MoveTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "DELETE" and toint(HttpStatusCode) == 403
| project DelTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url
| join kind=inner moves on SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url
| where MoveTime between (DelTime .. DelTime + win)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', MoveTime, DelTime)
| project DelTime, MoveTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url
| order by MoveTime desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method IN ("DELETE","MOVE") by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.status span=1s | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | eval isDenyDelete=if(http_method="DELETE" AND status==403,1,0), isMove=if(http_method="MOVE" AND (status==201 OR status==204),1,0) | stats max(eval(if(isDenyDelete==1,_time,null()))) as delTime max(eval(if(isMove==1,_time,null()))) as moveTime values(status) as statuses by src, dest, url | where isnotnull(delTime) AND isnotnull(moveTime) AND moveTime>=delTime AND (moveTime-delTime)<=60 | eval delaySec=moveTime-delTime | sort - moveTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method IN ("DELETE","MOVE") by _time, Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.status span=1s | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | eval isDenyDelete=if(http_method="DELETE" AND status==403,1,0), isMove=if(http_method="MOVE" AND (status==201 OR status==204),1,0) | stats max(eval(if(isDenyDelete==1,_time,null()))) as delTime max(eval(if(isMove==1,_time,null()))) as moveTime values(status) as statuses by src, dest, url | where isnotnull(delTime) AND isnotnull(moveTime) AND moveTime>=delTime AND (moveTime-delTime)<=60 | eval delaySec=moveTime-delTime | sort - moveTime
WebDAV MOVE with Overwrite:T header (destructive RemoveAll on destination) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the second, more destructive bypass path: a WebDAV MOVE carrying the 'Overwrite: T' header, which makes golang.org/x/net/webdav RemoveAll the existing destination before renaming — clobbering a pre-existing victim file even under --no-delete. Requires WAF/proxy header capture. Rationale: Targets the exact header the advisory names as the overwrite mechanism ('with Overwrite: T it additionally performs an explicit RemoveAll on the destination'). MOVE+Overwrite:T is the destructive-clobber variant and is not a shape normal clients emit against a read-controlled share.
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • macOS Finder / Windows mini-redirector legitimately sending Overwrite:T on renames against an intentionally writable WebDAV share
  • Sync clients (Cyberduck, davfs2) that default Overwrite:T on rename
  • Proxy not capturing request headers → query silently returns nothing (coverage gap, not a benign hit)
  • A goshs instance run without --no-delete where overwrite is expected behaviour
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the target DestinationHostName is a goshs --no-delete instance and read the Destination header to see which existing file was RemoveAll'd. 2) Contain: block the SourceIP and restrict the WebDAV port; recover the clobbered file from backup/snapshot. 3) Hunt: correlate to host-side FileDeleted+FileWritten to the same path by the goshs process, and search other goshs hosts for MOVE+Overwrite:T from the same client.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "MOVE"
| where Message has "Overwrite: T" or Message has "Overwrite:T" or DeviceCustomString1 has "Overwrite" or RequestContext has "Overwrite"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message, DeviceCustomString1
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable goshs exposure: process launched with --webdav and --no-delete (<= v2.1.3) AIWeaponization High
Inventory/exposure hunt for the vulnerable configuration itself: any goshs process started with both --webdav and --no-delete is exploitable by CVE-2026-64863 until upgraded past v2.1.3 (commit ba00ce3). Surfaces the attack surface before it is abused. Rationale: Uses the two flags the advisory names as the vulnerable combination (--webdav + --no-delete) plus the binary name goshs; projecting ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion lets an analyst confirm <= 2.1.3 without hand-editing the query.
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A goshs instance already upgraded past v2.1.3 where the flag combo is present but patched — check ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion
  • Internal-only goshs on a segmented network with no untrusted WebDAV clients (still vulnerable, lower priority)
  • Security team running goshs deliberately for a lab/CTF exercise
  • A renamed goshs binary — mitigated by also matching via the --no-delete/--webdav cmdline tokens
Suppression filter
| where ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion !in ("2.1.4","2.2.0") or isempty(ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the goshs version (ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion / --version) is <= 2.1.3 and determine whether the WebDAV port is reachable from untrusted networks. 2) Contain: upgrade goshs past 2.1.3, or firewall the WebDAV port to trusted hosts as an interim control. 3) Hunt: for every exposed instance, review WebDAV access logs for MOVE/Overwrite:T activity and host-side goshs file deletions to determine if the bypass was already used.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "goshs"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--webdav" and ProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessVersionInfoProductVersion, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has "goshs"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "--webdav" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "--no-delete"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
